inputs.cash_management_assets_note: Company-disclosed net debt of EUR 6,454m at 2026-06-30 nets ~EUR 331m of cash-management assets beyond the EUR 2,279m cash line (9,056 - 2,279 = 6,777 != 6,454); the disclosed figure is used. Capgemini's net-debt definition EXCLUDES lease liabilities, matching the lease treatment in the flows.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest received EUR 153m sits in FINANCING activities in Capgemini's cash flow statement (Annual_FY2025.txt line 23957), so it is not inside OCF and needs no strip from the owner-FCF base; the cash it is earned on is credited exactly once, in the net-debt bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement share-based payment add-back, EUR 266m (CAP.PA_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp; corroborated H1-2026 EUR 92m). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed; buybacks absorb settlement.
inputs.buyback_note: EUR 543m repurchased FY2025, EUR 315m in H1 2026 alone; EUR 545m of treasury shares cancelled in FY2025. The buyback is what keeps the count flat, funding the SBC charge already deducted from the flows.
inputs.share_count_basis: 168.3m = H1 FY2026 average shares outstanding (basic). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging performance-share dilution again via the ~174.4m diluted count would double-count (~6m of the diluted gap is unvested performance shares whose cost is the SBC line). Count has drifted DOWN 171m->168.3m since FY2023 on continuous buybacks.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at a EUR-built WACC of 8.0%: 10y Bund ~2.6% risk-free + ~5.0% euro ERP x beta ~1.2 (beta elevated by the sector-wide AI-disruption de-rating) = ~8.6% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~3.0% on BBB+ bonds; weights ~74% equity / 26% debt at the EUR ~18bn market cap vs EUR 6.5bn net debt. No small-cap illiquidity premium (EUR 18bn large cap, deep float). AI-disruption risk is charged ONCE, in the flows via the 30%-weighted bear scenario, not stacked on WACC (owner-fcf.md 7f); the same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios for the same reason. Post-WNS leverage is carried in the beta and in the EUR 6,454m bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: global IT-services operating company; asset-light, cash-generative). Fresh build - no prior DCF, no MEMORY.md entry. OWNER FCF BASIS: last_fcf = OCF 2,482 - capex 287 - lease principal repayments 296 - SBC 266 = EUR 1,633m FY2025. Capgemini's own 'organic FCF' APM (1,949) additionally nets interest and is NOT used: it is post-interest (double-counts financing against the net-debt bridge) and heavily H2-seasonal (H1-2026 was only EUR 37m - never annualize it). Naive OCF-capex (2,195) omits ~EUR 290m/yr of IFRS-16 lease principal. LEASE TREATMENT (B): lease cash charged in the flows (lease_cost_pct 1.3% of revenue), lease liabilities EXCLUDED from net debt - matching the company's own ex-lease net-debt definition; da_pct 1.8% is NON-lease D&A only (total FY2025 D&A 698 less ~300 ROU depreciation) so the lease cost is charged exactly once. MARGIN BASIS: statutory, NOT the 13.6-13.8% guided 'operating margin' APM, which excludes recurring restructuring (Fit-for-Growth ~EUR 700m cumulative FY2026-27), M&A amortization and SBC - H1 2026 statutory 7.3% vs APM 12.5%. The ebitda_margin_path is gross of SBC/lease/D&A and includes restructuring as an operating cost; FY2025 actual on this basis = 14.08% (statutory EBIT 2,199 + D&A 698 + SBC 266 = 3,163 on 22,465). Component build calibrated: FY0 replication gives EUR 1,634m vs 1,633m actual owner FCF. WC capture is NEGATIVE (-10% of revenue change): services receivables consume cash as revenue grows; this is not a deferred-revenue business.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.8% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 7.2% - the FY2020 base is an artificial trough (Altran goodwill funding + pension remeasurements cut equity 8,424->6,103). Neither is a usable forward driver.
historical_growth.notes: The 5yr/10yr revenue CAGRs (7.2%/6.6%) are ACQUISITION-DRIVEN (Altran 2020, WNS/Cloud4C 2025) and must not be mistaken for organic growth: organic/cc growth was negative-to-flat for six consecutive quarters Q1-2024 through Q3-2025, and ~5pts of the guided FY2026 +8.5-9.0% cc is WNS/Cloud4C scope. selected_growth_rate 3.0% is a through-cycle ORGANIC estimate (recent organic inflection ~+1-4%, book-to-bill 1.08x FY2025 / 1.04x H1-2026). Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on the adjusted series (OCF - capex - lease principal - SBC for the full history): 3yr NEGATIVE at -2.3% while reported FCF 3yr was -0.5% - SBC nearly doubled FY2021-2023 and lease charges grew, so reported FCF overstates the owner trend.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at guidance (+8.0% reported; ~5pts WNS/Cloud4C scope, FX ~-1pt), then growth fades to ~3% organic as the European recovery holds but AI compresses pricing on the staffing-pyramid work roughly in line with the productivity Capgemini passes through. Gross-EBITDA margin dips to 13.6% in FY2026 (Fit-for-Growth restructuring ~EUR 450m, statutory basis) then recovers to 14.8% - statutory EBIT ~10.6%, the middle of the FY2022-24 range, i.e. Fit-for-Growth pays for itself but no more, and ~EUR 150-200m/yr of restructuring remains a permanent cost of the model transition. Cash tax ramps 23%->26%. Owner-FCF margin matures at 8.1% by FY2035.
scenario_narratives.bull: Capgemini's Intelligent Operations bet works: WNS cross-sell (100+ joint pipeline), European sovereignty/defense spend and the agentic-AI transformation cycle make it a share gainer rather than a deflation victim. Growth holds 5-5.5% for three years post-WNS-lap, fading to 3%. Fit-for-Growth delivers the guided margin structure ON A STATUTORY BASIS: gross margin reaches 15.8% (statutory EBIT ~11.6%) as restructuring falls away after FY2027 and the pyramid reshapes toward outcome-based pricing.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI-deflation thesis is right - Capgemini's own URD concedes 'pricing to execution mismatches'. After the WNS lap (FY2026 +6.5%), agentic AI deflates billable hours faster than volume grows: revenue DECLINES 1-2.5%/yr for most of the decade (a real decline path, not slower growth). Pricing pressure plus under-utilized onshore Europe compresses gross margin 13.2%->11.0% (statutory EBIT ~6.8%) with restructuring permanent. Terminal growth 0%. The EUR 6.5bn net debt and goodwill > equity (EUR 14.7bn vs 11.6bn at Jun-2026) make this scenario a deleveraging grind with likely impairments - equity survives but compounds nothing.

entry_price.method: Price at which base/bull/bear interim owner FCF plus a terminal value REBUILT AT THE 15% HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_N), Gordon binds in all three) minus net debt returns 15% IRR over 10 years; probability-weighted across scenarios. The EUR 6,454m net debt deduction is why the entry prices sit so far below intrinsic value - a levered slow-grower priced for a 15% equity IRR is worth little more than its interim cash flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N)). The 8% row is the model WACC and ties to valuation.base.intrinsic_value; the 15% row ties to entry_price.base. At EUR 107.25 the market price implies a ~10.3% IRR on the base-case flows.

sensitivity.note: Base scenario. Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth. Flat rows at WACC 6-8% are the 15x terminal FCF cap binding regardless of terminal growth - the cap, not Gordon, sets the terminal value there.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (house default 15%): the AI-deflation risk is structural, conceded in Capgemini's own URD risk factors, already visible in peers' de-ratings and in A&T's sub-5% growth - and it coincides with peak leverage (net debt ~3x in 18 months) and goodwill (14.7bn) exceeding equity (11.6bn), so the downside path has a balance-sheet amplifier. Bull cut to 20%: it needs several independent things right at once (WNS synergies, statutory-basis margin delivery that H1-2026 Continental Europe contradicts, sovereignty spend materializing, AI net-positive). Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: Negative band position: EUR 107.25 sits BELOW even the house (fully-SBC-expensed) weighted IV of EUR 132.13, let alone the street basis EUR 158.14. Capgemini's SBC is modest (1.2% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow; the market is not arguing about SBC treatment here, it is pricing a heavier AI-deflation scenario than the 30% bear weight.

sanity_check.basis: Dec-close Yahoo monthly prices 2015-2025 aligned to the Dec-31 FY end. P/E on statutory EPS (IFRS2 - SBC already expensed on both sides). EV/EBITDA on post-lease-cost EBITDA (statutory operating profit + D&A - lease principal for IFRS16 years 2019+) against ex-lease net debt, matching the model's lease treatment. Net debt is the company APM for FY2021-25, debt-minus-cash before (FY2020 row overstates ND slightly by including lease liabilities in TotalDebt). D&A estimated at 3.2% of revenue for FY2020-23 where the KPI table has gaps.

implied_multiples.basis: Base IV EUR 153.79 x 168.3m shares = EUR 25.9bn equity, EUR 32.3bn EV, against FY2026E: revenue ~24,262, post-lease/post-SBC EBITDA ~2,717, net income ~1,512 (statutory EBIT 2,281 less ~180 net interest, 28% ETR), equity attributable 11,615 (Jun-2026).

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Every implied base-case multiple sits BELOW its 10-year average and inside the 10-year range: P/E 17.1x vs avg 19.5x (range 12.6-28.7), EV/EBITDA 11.9x vs avg 12.5x (9.9-17.4), P/Sales 1.07x vs avg 1.32x (0.99-1.83), P/B 2.23x vs avg 2.63x (1.76-3.93). The +43% base upside therefore does not require any multiple the stock has not routinely commanded - it requires only a partial reversal of the ~30% AI-fear de-rating (2025 closed at 13.9x P/E, the low end of a decade). The tension: those 10-year averages were set in a pre-generative-AI world; if the de-rating is the market correctly repricing a structurally deflating industry, the historical band is the wrong yardstick. That possibility is priced through the 30% bear weight (IV EUR 59.08), not by capping the base case.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required. Discipline retained anyway: terminal value uses a 15x owner-FCF cap (below the 20x house default, reflecting a structurally slower business), and the cap - not Gordon - binds the base and bull terminal values.
sanity_check.note: Owner-FCF multiples here will not match Yahoo/screener figures, which ignore the lease-principal and SBC adjustments.

valuation_philosophy.model: Owner-FCF component DCF on a strict statutory basis: SBC expensed and count flat, IFRS-16 lease principal charged in the flows against an ex-lease net-debt bridge, restructuring treated as a recurring operating cost (the 13.6-13.8% guided 'operating margin' APM is never used - the 5.2pp H1-2026 gap between it and the 7.3% statutory margin is the single most likely way to overvalue this company).
valuation_philosophy.central_tension: Capgemini trades at the bottom of its own 10-year multiple range after a ~30% de-rating, while guidance was RAISED in July 2026. Either the market is over-discounting AI deflation against still->1.0x book-to-bill and a raised outlook (the base/bull read: weighted IV EUR 132 vs price EUR 107), or the de-rating is the market correctly pricing the structural end of the billable-hours pyramid - in which case the decade of 19.5x average P/E is a dead benchmark. The model does not pick a side by fiat: the bear case is a genuine decline path (revenue shrinking 1-2.5%/yr, statutory EBIT to ~6.8%, IV EUR 59) weighted at 30%, double the house default, because Capgemini's own URD concedes the mechanism and peak leverage plus goodwill>equity amplify it.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: Bear weight rises if organic growth (ex-WNS scope) turns negative again post-lap, if A&T pricing per FTE visibly deflates, or if the FY2026 statutory margin misses despite the APM holding. Bull weight rises on evidence Fit-for-Growth converts to STATUTORY margin (restructuring actually tapering after FY2027), WNS synergies quantified and delivered, and deleveraging back toward ~1x EBITDA.
valuation_philosophy.verdict: At EUR 107.25 the price implies ~10.3% IRR on the base case - cheap versus an 8% WACC, but well short of the 15% hurdle (weighted entry EUR 46 - the leverage makes hurdle-rate entry nearly unreachable). A holdable fair-value-discount name, not a deep-value entry.

methodology: Owner-FCF component DCF per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf.md, sections 1-7: 10-year explicit horizon, three scenarios at a single EUR 8.0% WACC (risk charged once, in the flows), terminal = max(0, min(Gordon, 15x FCF_N)), entry price with TV rebuilt at the 15% hurdle. Base year FY2025; anchors refreshed to the H1-2026 balance sheet (2026-06-30).
